# Chapter Nine: Boom

Patricia awoke about 100 feet from the door to the garage, she could see the fire spreading from the entrance of the attached garage to the main house, half of the actual house was gone, it was a hole where it had been and she could see the second floor and part of the attic as it was exposed to the outside. She pulled a large piece of wood out of her abdomen and grunted with pain. She had to see who was alive. She tried to raise to her feet but Vertigo got the better of her and she slipped back down into a sitting position.

Suddenly Marcus was there with Timothy and Patricia Both the younger wolfs were helping her up, Marcus was saying something about the woods and then he was gone, back towards the house. She couldn’t make out his words before he left but the other two were urging her towards the wooded area, they kept a van there in case they needed to get away. But wait, where was Sowain and Brock, surely they were coming too. She pushed off the other two as she waited to see if Marcus returned. It seemed forever before Marcus came out of the house carrying a bloodied and battered Sowain. “Where is Brock?” she almost yelled as her hearing was pretty much toasted. “Couldn’t find him” Marcus said like he was under water and shouting upward.

The younger wolves looked off towards the distance as if hearing something, Police or fire trucks of course someone would have seen and heard that and called. Patricia allowed herself to be escorted towards the van and into it. Within a few moments the group was moving away towards Virginia. Sowain whispered something to Timothy who gave something that sounded like an address. Marcus nodded and then the blackness of sleep crept into Patricia as she slipped into unconsciousness, her body needing to regenerate.

Marcus

He drove down 95 towards Fredericksburg, still playing the whole thing through his head, he knew it had something to do with their mission, the timing was too perfect. He had been about to enter the Garage when the door suddenly flew towards him knocking him back and probably saving his life in the process. The door was a large metal security door they had installed to ensure no one could enter into the house through the garage easily. It had taken the blast full on and aside from warping the door was intact which in turn aside from a few broken ribs and at the very least a cracked collar bone was no worse for wear.

Both Rebecca and Timothy had still been in the TV room on the opposite side of the house and had, aside from getting thrown from the couch been hurt. Sowain was another story, Marcus wasn’t sure how the old man survived it but he had found him half in the fireplace in his office, He was in bad shape and still didn’t look good, he would have to shift soon to better heal the wounds.

The only one unaccounted for was Brock, and his bike was missing as well. Marcus wouldn’t believe even Brock was capable of doing something like this to his own pack, sure the guy was a weasel but he had been with them for decades, they were a family. Marcus then thought about the mission, did Brock have something vested in this human dying or was he doing the bidding of another, someone who wanted them out of the way allowing access to the human. Too many questions and no answers. Timothy had given him an address; one he had not known but apparently Sowain had whispered before passing out. So he drove, as fast as he could they had to get distance and get whole, something wasn’t right and they still could be in danger.

Brock

Brock gunned his motorcycle down the highway headed for Annapolis. He was sure Sowain would be dead by now, He had planted the charge in the garage literally right under his office, if he was lucky the fact that his motorcycle wouldn’t be noticed missing, if so it could be explained, he was sure, once Sowain’s Sire declared him Alpha of the pack, they would have to listen, they would have to obey. It was going to be okay, he just had to reach Annapolis.

About an hour later he pulled into the parking lot to the docks night had settled on the area and Brock could see the lights up and down the Chesapeake, standing in the middle of the parking lot was a man in biker leathers and a 1970 pan head. He just stood there admiring the bay, like a traveler would as he was passing through the area.

Brock pulled up and got off his own Dyna-Glide he strolled up and stood next to the man, but just a little behind him in deference to his age and position. Brock didn’t know how old the man was, but he was Sowain’s sire which made him at least as old as the country he was standing on, if not much older he went by the name Martin, but Brock knew that like Sowain the older ones changed them often to both hide from other pacts and to blend in with the human world. “I did it Martin, I kept them from going to the mission, I took care of Sowain as well, So we are good right” he said the words rushing out a statement of pride in completing his mission.

“Martin just stood there admiring the bay “You know there was a time when this bay was filled with tall ships, as men sailed up towards Annapolis with Spice and trade goods, the site was breathtaking” he said softly as he stared into the distance. Brock stood there for near 10 minutes before he finally lost patience “So we are solid with our deal right?” he asked eyeing Martin. The man sighed and turned towards Brock, “You were asked to delay them, not kill them, nor were you asked in any way to harm Sowain, what were you thinking” he said shaking his head as if scolding a dog for pooping on the carpet. Brock began to explain but before he could utter a word Martins hand shot out and separated Brock’s head from his shoulders in light swing like you would swat at a fly annoying you. It took a few moments for the head to actually realize it was no longer attached the man stepped over and picked it up gently

“You don’t get given a pack, you earn one Brock, and you were never going to earn one, you are too weak, you are fortunate my spawn survived, he is weak and hurt but alive, I can feel it. So I give you a quick death as you were only an annoyance, but one who did his job, thought as hap hazard as that was.” Martin dropped the head and brushed his hands on his pants. A dark sedan pulled up behind the bike and two large men in casual attire got out and strolled over to the man. “Ensure the body is taken care of, and then get me a report from the crew on the situation in Gaithersburg, I have not heard back and it’s been ample time” Both men nodded and began to gather up the body. As the man just stood there, admiring the bay “Tall ships indeed” he smiled to himself.
